important.name: Already-present route credits any change to a no_change file, including another issue edit
important.summary:
_present_files/_counts resolve an issue whose entries edited nothing once any own file listed under no_change is in changed, whatever changed it. A fixer owning I2 and I3 on a.py that edits a.py for I3 and records I2 as no_change [a.py] because it judged I2 wrong now gets I2 auto-RESOLVED with false already-present evidence. Before this PR that raised the no-fixed-entry problem. The what text is never checked, so the fixer rule at pr_review.py:1687-1689 does not bound the route.

Also (overall): _Planned.owned (review_merge.py:699-709) now lets a split part list the whole rest of the fixer's file set, other issues' files included, and _own_file_problem (767-773) skips split issues, while _counts (799-801) accepts any non-empty e.files. Trace: M1 split over a.py/b.py; w1_fix_1 owns {M1:[a.py], I1:[t.py]}; entry M1 files=[t.py] (edited for I1), no_change=[a.py]; w1_fix_2 entry M1 no_change=[b.py]. Every check passes, coverage is complete, and M1 is RESOLVED with plain fixed evidence although neither a.py nor b.py changed. Before this PR t.py was an other issue's part, not in _extra_files, so the entry was rejected. It also bypasses the new already-present rule, which requires an own file in `changed`. No test covers the negative case; test_split_part_may_list_another_issues_file only exercises an entry that also edits a.py.

Also (overall): _present_files (review_merge.py:791-796) counts an own file listed under no_change as proof of a fix whenever it is in `changed`, whoever changed it. Its docstring claims the file is one 'that no entry of this closeout edited', but nothing checks that: if M1 and I2 both live in a.py (one fixer), a fixer that edits a.py for I2 and lists M1's a.py under no_change resolves M1 as already present with no M1 fix. The fixer rule (pr-fixer.md:54-56, pr_review.py:1687-1689) asks for `already present` in `what`, but closeout never reads `what`, so a cited-only entry turns into an already-present resolution too. test_split_issue_already_present_resolves shows this: both entries say 'only cited as context' and M1 still resolves as already present. This removes the guard that test_every_part_no_change_is_problem used to enforce, and the PR rewrote that test (changed=set()) to fit.

Also (tests): TestCloseoutFixAlreadyPresent only proves a non-own changed file (t.py) is not enough. It never covers the case where the issue's own file changed because a different issue's validated entry edited it in the same closeout. In review_merge._present_files (lines 791-796), any own file listed under no_change that is in `changed` counts as 'already present'. With M1 and M2 both on a.py, an M2 entry editing a.py plus an M1 entry `{"what": "cited only", "no_change": ["a.py"]}` resolves M1 as RESOLVED '(already present: a.py changed since build)'. That turns a 'needs no edit / cited only' report into a resolution on unrelated edits, and no test pins either the intended or the actual behavior.

Also (tests): _present takes `issue: Optional[Dict[str, object]] = None` and documents it as the default M1 on a.py, but all three callers (lines 1099, 1109, 1115) omit it. The parameter is dead.
fix: In _present_files, ignore own files that a validated entry of another issue in this closeout lists under files.
Require an already-present marker in the no_change entry what text before _counts accepts it.

Make _counts require an own-file edit: `own = planned.own.get(issue_id, set()); return any(set(e.files) & own for e in entries) or bool(_present_files(...))`, and use the same predicate in _fixed_evidence (818-827) for the already-present note; add a test where a split entry edits only another issue's file and expects the `no fixed entry edited a file` problem.
Extend _own_file_problem to split issues (an entry that edits files must edit one of the issue's own files, its part or the rest of the issue's planned files).

In _present_files, drop own files that an accepted entry of another issue lists under `files` in this closeout, so that case falls back to the problem plus the resolvable_hints `--resolved` route, where the developer verifies the fix; fix the docstring to match.

Require the entry's `what` to contain `already present` (the fixer rule's marker) before _present_files counts its no_change files, and add a test where a cited-only entry with a changed own file stays a problem.

Add a negative test: review with M1 and M2 on a.py, one fixer, M2 fixed with files=[a.py], M1 with no_change=[a.py] and changed={a.py}; assert M1 keeps the 'no fixed entry edited a file' problem. Then make _present_files ignore files that a validated entry of another issue lists under `files` in this closeout.
If the sibling-edit resolution is intended, pin it with a test and say so in the apply_closeout docstring and the fixer rule at scripts/pr_review.py:1687-1689.
Drop the `issue` parameter and build `_review(_issue("M1", "a.py"))` directly; update the docstring to match.

important.name: 'any problem of an id stops once it resolves' overstates the code
important.summary:
SKILL.md now says 'any problem of an id stops once that id ends a closeout RESOLVED or CLOSED_NO_ACTION by any path, the same closeout included'. apply_closeout (review_merge.py:995) drops only the `rejected` list (entry rejections from _check_entry plus coverage problems from _apply_fixed). The problems from _apply_bubbles (_bubble_problem: '<id> (<fixer>): bubbled id not assigned to this fixer' / 'not a planned fixer; <id> not bubbled') and from _apply_resolved ('<id>: none of its files changed since build') sit in the unfiltered `problems` list and keep closeout blocked even when that id is RESOLVED in the same run. The fix reports stay on disk, so rerunning closeout as the doc suggests reproduces the same [blocked] line. The apply_closeout docstring (review_merge.py:962-965, 974) makes the same promise for bubbles, and the code does not keep it.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:842-844 sends 'a partially fixed or rejected-entry problem' to a bare `waves` rerun. SKILL.md:845-847 then says a `hint:` line means 'rerun closeout --resolved instead of another wave'. resolvable_hints (review_merge.py:1002-1016) emits a hint for every non-partially-fixed problem whose issue has a changed own file. Most rejected entries edited files (outside the set, or a non-own file), so they usually get both instructions. Which one wins is only implied by sentence order. The doc also gives no route for a fix that was already present at build_head (no own file changed): 'no fixed entry edited a file' persists, no hint fires, --resolved fails with 'none of its files changed', and the only exit is --closed.
fix: Narrow the SKILL.md sentence back to what the code does: 'a rejected-entry or partially-fixed problem of an id stops once that id ends a closeout RESOLVED or CLOSED_NO_ACTION by any path, the same closeout included', and match the apply_closeout docstring to it.

Or make the code keep the promise: have _apply_bubbles return (id, problem) pairs and route them through the same `resolved` filter as `rejected` at review_merge.py:995 (and do the same for _apply_resolved problems of an id that ends up RESOLVED), then add a test where a bubble problem is superseded by a valid entry.

Rewrite SKILL.md:842-848 so the precedence is explicit: an id named by a `hint:` line goes to `closeout --resolved` after verifying the fix; other partially-fixed or rejected-entry ids go to a bare `waves`. Add one clause: a fix already present at build_head (no file changed) is closed with `--closed ID="already fixed before build"`.

minor.name: pr-fixer 'already present' rule omits which no_change files count
minor.summary: pr-fixer.md:54-56 (and the matching brief rule at pr_review.py:1687-1689) tell the fixer to 'list the issue's files that hold it under no_change' and say closeout resolves once one of those files changed. In the code a no_change file outside the fixer's owned set rejects the whole entry (_entry_problem, review_merge.py:678-680). For a split part, another fixer's part file falls outside that set (_Planned.owned). Only the issue's own files (primary or also) count as 'present' (_present_files, review_merge.py:796), so a fix that sits in a widened test or named doc path never resolves. A split issue also still needs every planned part covered. A haiku fixer following the literal text can list another fixer's part file, and the entry is then rejected.
fix: Reword pr-fixer.md:54-56 and pr_review.py:1687-1689 to: 'list the issue's own files (primary or also) in your part or file set that hold it under no_change ...; closeout resolves it once one of those files changed since the build (a split issue still needs every part covered)'.

minor.name: No documented route for a fix that predates build_head
minor.summary: pr-fixer.md:54-56 tells a fixer to edit nothing when the fix is already present. If the fix was already in the tree at build (stale finding), no listed file is in `changed`. Closeout then raises 'no fixed entry edited a file (only no_change files)', and no hint fires because resolvable_hints needs a changed file. SKILL.md:829-831 and the fixer rule cover only the changed-since-build case, so the operator is left without a next step. The right route is `closeout --closed ID=...`.
fix: Add to SKILL.md after line 831: 'When the fix predates build_head (no listed file changed), close the id with `closeout --closed <id>="already in place at build"`'; optionally have resolvable_hints emit a `--closed` hint for a no_change-only problem whose files are unchanged.

fix: Assert the M3 evidence exactly, e.g. that it ends with '- guard; cited; already there' and does not contain '(already present', so the test pins the cross-issue-file acceptance it actually exercises.
Or reword the docstring so it says M3 resolves through wave 1's edit and waves 2-3 add no_change coverage.
